claim: Angiogenesis requires the temporal coordination of the proliferation and the migration of endothelial cells.
source: Angiogenesis requires the temporal coordination of the proliferation and the migration of endothelial cells.
evidence: This is a foundational statement in the abstract that sets up the research question.

claim: A microRNA network contributes to the observed down- and upregulation of proliferative and migratory genes during angiogenesis.
source: We described a microRNA network which contributes to the observed down- and upregulation of proliferative and migratory genes, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by the network analysis and experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Global analysis of miRNA–target gene interactions identified two sub-network modules with opposite regulatory patterns.
source: Global analysis of miRNA–target gene interactions identified two sub-network modules, the first organized in upregulated miRNAs connected with downregulated target genes and the second with opposite features.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by Figure 4 showing the network structure.

claim: Gain- and loss-of-function approaches targeting miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p impaired angiogenesis.
source: Gain- and loss-of-function approaches targeting these microRNAs impaired angiogenesis, suggesting that these modules are instrumental to the temporal coordination of endothelial migration and proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E-F demonstrating effects on sprouting.

claim: miR-29a-3p and its targets belong to a selective biomarker that identifies colorectal cancer patients responding to anti-angiogenic treatments.
source: Interestingly, miR-29a-3p and its targets belong to a selective biomarker that is able to identify colorectal cancer patients who are responding to anti-angiogenic treatments.
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 9D with bevacizumab-responding patients.

claim: The expansion of a vascular network through sprouting angiogenesis requires coordinated control of many cellular functions.
source: The expansion of a vascular network through the sprouting angiogenesis (SA) process requires a coordinated control of many cellular functions, including the activation of quiescent endothelial cells (ECs), cell protrusion, basal lamina and extracellular matrix degradation, cell migration and proliferation, deposition of new basement membrane, cell junctions and cell polarity alteration (Carmeliet and Jain, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: During sprouting angiogenesis, ECs dynamically switch from a tip phenotype to a stalk cell state.
source: In particular, during SA, ECs dynamically switch from a tip phenotype, which guides the network expansion, to a stalk cell state that is characterized by active proliferation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about angiogenesis cited in the introduction.

claim: VEGF-A is the most prominent cytokine that activates a genetic program sustaining angiogenesis.
source: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-A (VEGF-A) is the most prominent cytokine that activates a genetic program that sustains this morphogenetic process (Simons et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: Transcriptomic analysis of tip and stalk cells showed differential expression of molecular determinants.
source: Transcriptomic analysis of tip and stalk cells isolated from the retinal vascular plexus showed differential expression of molecular determinants, represented by genes that are involved in extracellular matrix remodeling for tip cells and that encode components of the Notch signaling pathway for stalk cells (del Toro et al., 2010; Strasser et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: EC fate decision towards tip or stalk cell phenotype is affected by VEGF-A gradient concentration and VEGF receptor expression levels.
source: It also has been proposed that the EC fate decision towards the tip or stalk cell phenotype is affected by VEGF-A gradient concentration in the surrounding extracellular matrix and by VEGF receptors expression levels (Gerhardt et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: MicroRNAs extensively modulate gene expression at the post-transcriptional level by targeting mRNAs.
source: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a class of small non-coding RNAs that extensively modulate gene expression at the post-transcriptional level by targeting the mRNAs of protein-coding genes, directing their repression through mRNA degradation or (to a lesser extent) inhibition of protein translation (Guo et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about miRNA function supported by citation.

claim: One of the first functions attributed to miRNAs was the control of developmental processes.
source: Interestingly, one of the first functions attributed to miRNAs was the control of developmental processes in which a morphogen gradient directs cell fate by activating specific genetic programs (Inui et al., 2012; Ivey and Srivastava, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: miRNAs are an integral part of the regulatory network that allows transitions between different cell states.
source: In this scenario, miRNAs are an integral part of the regulatory network that allows transitions between different cell states (Hornstein and Shomron, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: A role for miRNAs in ECs biology and vascular development has been established by inhibition of Dicer and Drosha.
source: A role for miRNAs in ECs biology and vascular development has been established in vitro and in vivo by inhibition of two endonucleases that are required for mature miRNAs generation, namely Dicer and Drosha (Ha and Kim, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Reduction in miRNA levels resulted in alteration of EC sprouting ability and impaired postnatal angiogenesis.
source: The consequent reduction in the level of miRNAs resulted in alteration of several key properties of ECs, including their sprouting ability (Kuehbacher et al., 2007), and impaired postnatal angiogenesis (Suárez et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: miR-15a and miR-16 repress VEGF expression.
source: Several studies have demonstrated that miR-15a and miR-16, among other miRNAs, repress VEGF expression (Chamorro-Jorganes et al., 2011; Yin et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: miR-126 promotes VEGF signaling by targeting PIK3R2.
source: whereas miR-126 promotes VEGF signaling by targeting the downstream effector PIK3R2 (Fish et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: miR-27b and miR-221 are required for tip cell specification.
source: Furthermore, miR-27b and miR-221 are required for tip cell specification (Biyashev et al., 2012; Nicoli et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: RNA-sequencing technology allowed generation of complete annotation of miRNAs expressed by cultured human ECs.
source: Recently, RNA-sequencing (RNAseq) technology allowed the generation of a complete annotation of the miRNAs that are expressed by two-dimensional cultured human ECs in normal (Kuosmanen et al., 2017) or hypoxic (Voellenkle et al., 2012) conditions.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: VEGF-A induces the tip phenotype of endothelial cells in the 3D spheroid model.
source: VEGF-A induces the tip phenotype of endothelial cells in a 3D model of sprouting angiogenesis
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing tip marker expression in Figure 1B.

claim: Expression analysis identified 3071 differentially expressed genes in SPHV compared to SPHC.
source: Expression analysis of protein-coding genes identified 3071 differentially expressed (DE) genes in SPHV compared to SPHC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by the referenced figure showing the heatmap.

claim: VEGFR2 was upregulated in SPHV compared to SPHC.
source: Upregulation of VEGFR2, the major VEGF signal transducer, was validated by real-time PCR and Western blot analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental validation data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: A general upregulation of tip marker genes and downregulation of stalk marker genes was observed in SPHV compared to SPHC.
source: By looking at the expression of known tip and stalk cell markers (De Bock et al., 2013; del Toro et al., 2010; Strasser et al., 2010), we observed a general upregulation of tip marker genes and a downregulation of stalk marker genes in the comparison between SPHV and SPHC (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap in Figure 1B and citations to previous literature defining these markers.

claim: EC sprouts strongly expressed DLL4 and CXCR4.
source: Although the EC sprouts strongly expressed DLL4 and CXCR4, cells in which the Notch reporter was activated were present only occasionally, so ECs largely acquired a tip-cell phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Manipulation of the Notch pathway by DAPT increased sprouting.
source: Furthermore, manipulation of the Notch pathway by the γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT or by exogenous DLL4 resulted in increased or reduced sprouting, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Manipulation of the Notch pathway by exogenous DLL4 reduced sprouting.
source: Furthermore, manipulation of the Notch pathway by the γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT or by exogenous DLL4 resulted in increased or reduced sprouting, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: GSEA confirmed upregulation of VEGF-A responder genes in SPHV compared to SPHC.
source: When comparing SPHV with SPHC, this analysis confirmed the upregulation of known VEGF-A responder genes ('VEGF-A UP')
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: GSEA revealed positive enrichment of gene sets representing Translation, Cell adhesion molecules, Integrin pathway, Extracellular matrix organization, and Collagen formation in SPHV.
source: and revealed a positive enrichment of gene sets that are representative of several biological pathways and classes of molecules, including 'Translation', 'Cell adhesion molecules', 'Integrin pathway', 'Extracellular matrix organization', and 'Collagen formation'.
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: GSEA showed enrichment of Oxidative phosphorylation and Lysosome pathways in SPHV.
source: Other representative enriched pathways included 'Oxidative phosphorylation' and 'Lysosome' (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: GSEA showed a strongly negative enrichment score for cell-cycle-controlling genes in SPHV.
source: Nonetheless, and in agreement with the non-proliferating tip cell phenotype, GSEA showed a strongly negative enrichment score (ES) for cell-cycle-controlling genes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA plot shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 52 genes out of 113 cell cycle genes were differentially expressed in SPHV compared to SPHC, of which 50 were downregulated.
source: Indeed, when looking at the expression levels of genes belonging to the 'cell cycle' KEGG pathway (Kanehisa et al., 2016), expression analysis showed that 52 genes out of 113 were DE in SPHV compared to SPHC, of which 50 were downregulated (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap in Figure 2B and citation to the KEGG database.

claim: Hypergeometric test confirmed statistically significant over-representation of downregulated cell cycle genes among all DE genes.
source: Hypergeometric test confirmed a statistically significant over-representation of this subset of genes among all the DE genes (P = 7.40x10-5).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result supporting the enrichment of cell cycle genes.

claim: Only cyclin D2 (CCND2) and cyclin E1 (CCNE1) were upregulated among cell cycle genes.
source: Only cyclin D2 (CCND2) and cyclin E1 (CCNE1), two genes belonging to the cyclin family and participating in the G1phase of the cell cycle, were upregulated.
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GSEA showed negative enrichment score for pyrimidine metabolism gene sets.
source: The finding that VEGF-A did not activate the proliferation of ECs and the accompanying DNA synthesis was also confirmed by the negative ES of gene sets that are representative of pyrimidine metabolism (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is supported by GSEA plot shown in Figure 2C.

claim: GSEA showed negative enrichment score for purine metabolism gene sets.
source: and, to a lesser extent, purine metabolism (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA plot shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A general downregulation of genes involved in de novo synthesis of nucleotides was observed.
source: Indeed, we observed a general downregulation of genes involved in de novo synthesis of nucleotides (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Downregulation of cyclin B1 gene was validated by real-time PCR.
source: Downregulations of the cyclin B1 gene and of IMPDH2, the rate-limiting enzyme in de novo guanine nucleotide biosynthesis, were validated by a real-time PCR assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Downregulation of IMPDH2 was validated by real-time PCR.
source: Downregulations of the cyclin B1 gene and of IMPDH2, the rate-limiting enzyme in de novo guanine nucleotide biosynthesis, were validated by a real-time PCR assay (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: VEGF-A stimulation decreased the activity of PPAT, ATIC, and CAD enzymes in the 3D model.
source: VEGF-A stimulation decreased the activity of these three enzymes in the 3D model (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is supported by enzymatic activity measurements shown in Figure 2E.

claim: PPAT, ATIC, and CAD enzyme activity significantly increased in 2D cultured ECs upon VEGF-A stimulation.
source: On the contrary, their activity significantly increased in a control experiment performed with ECs cultured in 2D conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by enzymatic activity measurements shown in the referenced figure.

claim: SPHC displayed a quiescent, non-proliferative status.
source: Measurement of the percentage of cells that entered the S phase of the cell cycle confirmed that SPHC displayed a quiescent, non-proliferative status
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: VEGF-A was not able to trigger cell proliferation in spheroids significantly within an 18-hr time frame.
source: and that VEGF-A was not able to trigger cell proliferation in spheroids significantly within an 18-hr time frame (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: VEGF-A activity on cell proliferation was evident in cells cultured in standard 2D conditions.
source: By contrast, VEGF-A activity on cell proliferation was well evident in cells cultured in standard 2D conditions, both in a proliferation assay and in a GSEA of the corresponding microarray data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay and GSEA data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: ECs that were mitotically inactivated by mitomycin C treatment maintained the ability to migrate and form endothelial sprouts.
source: Furthermore, ECs that were mitotically inactivated by mitomycin C treatment maintained the ability to migrate and to form endothelial sprouts (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by sprouting assay data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: In 3D conditions, early VEGF-A activity is primarily directed towards cell migration rather than cell proliferation.
source: Taken together, these observations indicate that, in 3D conditions, early VEGF-A activity is primarily directed towards cell migration rather than towards cell proliferation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from multiple experimental observations presented in Figure 2.

claim: 639 mature miRNAs were expressed by ECs across SPHC and SPHV conditions above the cutoff.
source: Analysis of the small-RNAs sequencing data allowed the annotation of 639 mature miRNAs that were expressed by ECs across the two experimental conditions (SPHC and SPHV), at levels above a fixed cutoff (raw counts = 5) (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is directly stated based on small RNA sequencing analysis.

claim: The frequency distribution of the correlator for conserved miRNA-target interactions showed significant enrichment in negative correlations.
source: The frequency distribution of the correlator for the conserved interactions subset showed a significant enrichment in negative correlations compared to that for the entire dataset (Figure 3B, blue line).
evidence: This is supported by the distribution plot shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Non-conserved miRNA-target interactions did not show any significant alteration in the correlator frequency distribution.
source: By contrast, the non-conserved interactions subset did not show any significant alteration in the correlator frequency distribution (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the distribution plot shown in the referenced figure.

claim: GSEA-based analysis identified five clusters of genesets representing distinct biological functions modulated during SA.
source: This analysis identified five clusters of genesets representing distinct biological functions that are modulated during SA, together with their associated miRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by the association matrix shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The global post-transcriptional regulatory network is composed of 149 miRNAs and 717 protein-coding genes connected by 1713 edges.
source: The resulting miRNA-centered co-expression network is composed of 149 miRNAs and 717 protein-coding genes connected by 1713 edges (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by the network visualization in Figure 4.

claim: The network is characterized by two individual components with opposite regulatory patterns.
source: This network is essentially characterized by two individual components: one representing upregulated miRNAs connected with downregulated target genes, and one representing downregulated miRNAs connected with upregulated target genes.
evidence: This is supported by the network structure shown in Figure 4.

claim: Degree distribution for both miRNAs and protein-coding genes observed a power-law behavior.
source: Degree distribution for both miRNAs (out-degree) and protein-coding genes (in-degree) observed a power-law behavior (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C), indicating that this network is compatible with the scale-free hypothesis, a typical feature of biological networks (Barabási and Pósfai, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by the cumulative distribution function plots in the referenced figures and citation to network theory.

claim: TAOK1 gene was the most targeted gene in the MAPK sub-network, being targeted by 11 different miRNAs.
source: The TAOK1 gene, whose protein product is a kinase that activates stress response (Raman et al., 2007), and MAPK1, whose protein product is ERK2, were the most targeted genes in this sub-network, being targeted by 11 and 7 different miRNAs, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by the MAPK sub-network shown in Figure 5A and citation about TAOK1 function.

claim: MAPK1 (ERK2) was targeted by 7 different miRNAs in the MAPK sub-network.
source: The TAOK1 gene, whose protein product is a kinase that activates stress response (Raman et al., 2007), and MAPK1, whose protein product is ERK2, were the most targeted genes in this sub-network, being targeted by 11 and 7 different miRNAs, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by the MAPK sub-network shown in Figure 5A.

claim: All components constituting the ERK module (C-Raf, MEK, and ERK2) were represented in the MAPK sub-network.
source: Notably, all components constituting the ERK module, namely C-Raf (RAF1), MEK (MAP2K1) and ERK2 (MAPK1), were represented.
evidence: This is supported by the MAPK sub-network shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Downregulation of RAF1, MAP2K1, MAPK1 and TAOK1 in SPHV compared to SPHC was validated by real-time PCR.
source: Downregulation of RAF1, MAP2K1, MAPK1 and TAOK1, and upregulation of MAPK14 in SPHV compared to SPHC, was validated by real-time PCR (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Upregulation of MAPK14 in SPHV compared to SPHC was validated by real-time PCR.
source: Downregulation of RAF1, MAP2K1, MAPK1 and TAOK1, and upregulation of MAPK14 in SPHV compared to SPHC, was validated by real-time PCR (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ERK activity decreases after VEGF treatment in the spheroid model.
source: Furthermore, ERK activity was measured in SPHC and SPHV by Meso Scale Technology (MSD) and expressed as P-ERK/total ERK ratio in order to take variations in total ERK expression into account. Figure 5C shows that ERK activity decreases after VEGF treatment.
evidence: This is supported by MSD measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Treatment with ERK inhibitor SCH 772984 did not have any effect on sprouting.
source: As shown in Figure 5D, treatment with the ERK inhibitor SCH 772984 did not have any effect on sprouting
evidence: This is supported by sprouting assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Treatment with p38MAPK inhibitor SB 202190 completely abrogated the ability of ECs to migrate and form sprouts.
source: By contrast, treatment with p38MAPK inhibitor SB 202190 completely abrogated the ability of ECs to migrate and to form sprouts.
evidence: This is supported by sprouting assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: DICER knock-down reduced sprouting to about 50% of control cells.
source: Cells in which DICER expression was knocked-down by a short-hairpin RNA (DICERKD) showed a reduction of sprouting to about 50% of that seen in cells transduced by non-targeting shRNA (DICERWT) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), in agreement with previous observations (Kuehbacher et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by sprouting assay data shown in the referenced figure and citation to previous work.

claim: RAF1, MAP2K1, MAPK1, TAOK1, and MAPK14 were upregulated in DICERKD spheroids compared to DICERWT.
source: Then, we measured RAF1, MAP2K1, MAPK1, TAOK1, and MAPK14 expression in SPHV generated with DICERWT or DICERKD cells by real-time PCR. All of these genes were upregulated in the DICERKD condition (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The amount of P-ERK increased in DICERKD spheroids.
source: The amount of P-ERK also increased in DICERKD spheroids (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by MSD measurements shown in Figure 6B.

claim: DICERKD spheroids treated with ERK inhibitor showed a further reduction of sprouting.
source: Nonetheless, DICERKD spheroids that were treated with the ERK inhibitor showed a further reduction of sprouting (Figure 6C,D)
evidence: This is supported by sprouting assay data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: GSEA showed higher expression of cell cycle and nucleotide metabolism genes in DICERKD spheroids compared to DICERWT spheroids stimulated with VEGF-A.
source: GSEA comparison showed levels of expression of 'cell cycle'- and 'metabolism of nucleotides'-related genes in DICERKDspheroids that were higher than those in DICERWT spheroids stimulated with VEGF-A (Figure 6E)
evidence: This is supported by GSEA plots shown in Figure 6E.

claim: DICERKD spheroids displayed a VEGF-A-dependent increase of cell proliferation compared to DICERWT spheroids.
source: DICERKD spheroids displayed a VEGF-A-dependent increase of cell proliferation compared to DICERWT spheroids, confirming that the removal of miRNAs allows activation of the proliferative pathway downstream of VEGF-A.
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: In 2D culture, DICERKD cells showed a reduced proliferative response to VEGF compared to DICERWT cells.
source: Interestingly, when the proliferation assay was performed on ECs cultured in 2D, DICERKD cells showed a reduced proliferative response to VEGF compared to DICERWT cells, suggesting that different miRNA activities are involved in the 2D or 3D environments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: miR-424–5p was upregulated and targeted 98 genes mainly related to intracellular signaling and cell cycle control.
source: miR-424–5 p was upregulated and targeted 98 genes, which were mainly related to intracellular signaling, including the MAPK pathway (Figure 5A) and cell cycle control (Figure 7A and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the network analysis shown in Figure 7A and the source data.

claim: miR-29a-3p was downregulated and controlled post-transcriptional regulation of 25 genes mostly related to extracellular matrix remodeling.
source: miR-29a-3p was downregulated and controlled the post-transcriptional regulation of 25 genes, mostly related to extracellular matrix remodeling (Figure 7B and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the network analysis shown in Figure 7B and the source data.

claim: For miR-424–5p, 97 out of 98 interactions were present in miRTarBase, TarBase, or starBase databases.
source: In particular, for miR-424–5 p, 97 out of 98 interactions were present in these databases (24 of them in all three databases, and 73 in one or two)
evidence: This validates the predicted interactions against experimentally supported databases.

claim: For miR-29a-3p, 23 out of 25 interactions were present in miRTarBase, TarBase, or starBase databases.
source: for miR-29a-3p, 23 out of 25 interactions were present in the databases (7 of them in all three databases, 16 in one or two) (Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This validates the predicted interactions against experimentally supported databases.

claim: RNAseq expression data for miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p in SPHC and SPHV were confirmed by real-time PCR.
source: RNAseq expression data for miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p in SPHC and SPHV were confirmed by real-time PCR analysis (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR validation data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Inhibition of the Notch pathway with DAPT increased the expression of miR-424–5p.
source: In fact, inhibition of the Notch pathway with DAPT, which increases sprouting (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), increased the expression of miR-424–5p
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Inhibition of the Notch pathway with DAPT reduced the expression of miR-29a-3p.
source: and reduced the expression of miR-29a-3p
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Treatment with exogenous DLL4 reduced the expression of miR-424–5p.
source: the opposite effect was obtained when spheroids were treated with exogenous DLL4 (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Treatment with exogenous DLL4 increased the expression of miR-29a-3p.
source: the opposite effect was obtained when spheroids were treated with exogenous DLL4 (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Both upregulation and downregulation of miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p impaired the ability of ECs to sprout.
source: Quantification of sprout areas (Figure 7F) indicated that both upregulation by miRNA mimics and downregulation by miRNA inhibitors of miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p impaired the ability of ECs to sprout
evidence: This is supported by sprouting assay data shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: Cells with altered expression of miR-424–5p or miR-29a-3p were impaired in reaching the tip cell position.
source: Figure 7—figure supplement 2 shows that cells with altered expression of miR-424–5p or miR-29a-3p were impaired in reaching the tip cell position.
evidence: This is supported by tip competition assay data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: miR-16–5p modulation did not affect sprouting.
source: Indeed, miR-16–5 p modulation did not affect sprouting (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is supported by sprouting assay data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p expression was significantly reduced in DICERKD spheroids compared to DICERWT spheroids.
source: miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p expression was significantly reduced in DICERKD spheroids compared to DICERWT spheroids (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H)
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Modulation of miR-424–5p resulted in alteration of P-ERK activity.
source: Furthermore, modulation of miR-424–5p, which is involved in the MAPK sub-network shown in Figure 5A, resulted in the alteration of P-ERK activity according to the bioinformatics prediction
evidence: This is supported by MSD measurements shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Modulation of miR-29a-3p did not affect P-ERK activity.
source: whereas modulation of miR-29a-3p, which is not involved in this network, was not effective (Figure 7—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by MSD measurements shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Treatment with miR-424–5p mimic reduced cell proliferation by 50% in 2D culture.
source: In a 2D VEGF-dependent cell proliferation assay, however, treatment with the miR-424–5p mimic was able to reduce cell proliferation by 50% (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The miR-424–5p mimic had a positive effect on cell migration in 2D culture.
source: When tested in a 2D VEGF-dependent cell migration experiment, the miR-424–5p mimic had a positive effect on cell migration
evidence: This is supported by migration assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The miR-29a-3p mimic had a negative effect on cell migration in 2D culture.
source: whereas the miR-29a-3p mimic had a negative effect
evidence: This is supported by migration assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Overexpression of miR-424–5p mimic reduced the expression of 10 predicted target genes.
source: Indeed, we were able to verify a reduction in the expression of target genes when the corresponding miRNA mimic was overexpressed (Figure 7H,I).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: Overexpression of miR-29a-3p mimic reduced the expression of 10 predicted target genes.
source: Indeed, we were able to verify a reduction in the expression of target genes when the corresponding miRNA mimic was overexpressed (Figure 7H,I).
evidence: This is supported by real-time PCR data shown in Figure 7I.

claim: 76 miRNAs showed altered expression upon up- or downmodulation of miR-424–5p or miR-29a-3p in at least two conditions.
source: The results indicate that 76 miRNAs showed altered expression (|∆∆Ct| > 2) upon up- or downmodulation of miR-424–5p or miR-29a-3p in at least two conditions (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by TaqMan array data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: 27 miRNAs that share common target genes with miR-424–5p or miR-29a-3p showed altered expression upon their modulation.
source: In particular, when the analysis was restricted to the subset of miRNAs that share common target genes with miR-424–5p or miR-29a-3p in the SA network, 27 of these miRNAs showed altered expression (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by TaqMan array data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Expression of miR-29a-3p targets showed significant positive enrichment in CRC samples with high endothelial score.
source: When GSEA was used to correlate the different miRNA-target gene subsets obtained from the network analysis (Figure 4—source data 1) with CRC samples, we observed a significant positive enrichment for the miR-29a-3p-targets subset (Figure 9A)
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Average expression of upregulated genes from the network showed significant positive correlation with endothelial score in CRC samples.
source: Furthermore, average expression in CRC samples of the genes that were present in the network analysis and that are upregulated in SPHV (upregulated module, Figure 9—source data 1) also showed a significant positive correlation with endothelial score (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 9B.

claim: GSEA revealed significant enrichment of the upregulated module in CRC samples with high endothelial score.
source: Likewise, GSEA analysis in which the endothelial score was used as phenotype classifier revealed a significant enrichment of the upregulated module (Figure 9C)
evidence: This is supported by GSEA plot shown in Figure 9C.

claim: A core gene set of 58 genes was identified that are coherently regulated in vitro and in vivo.
source: and allowed the identification of a core gene set of 58 genes that are coherently regulated in vitro and in vivo (Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: This is derived from GSEA analysis shown in Figure 9C.

claim: The core subset of the upregulated gene module was significantly enriched in bevacizumab-responding CRC patients.
source: Indeed, the core subset of the upregulated gene module was significantly enriched in bevacizumab-responding patients (Figure 9D)
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 9D using patient response data.

claim: The spheroid model at the 18-hour timepoint represents the early phase of VEGF-A response involving activation of quiescent ECs and differentiation to tip cells.
source: Altogether, these observations indicate that this sprouting model can be used, at this specific developmental time point, to represent the early phase of VEGF-A response that involves activation of quiescent ECs and differentiation to tip cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from multiple observations about tip marker expression and lack of stalk cells.

claim: The onset of vascular sprouting depends on migration of existing ECs and does not require EC proliferation.
source: The observation that these two fundamental VEGF-A downstream pathways might not be synchronous in tip cells is in agreement with earlier studies on pathophysiological angiogenesis, in which it was demonstrated that the onset of vascular sprouting depends on the migration of existing ECs and does not require EC proliferation (Ausprunk and Folkman, 1977; Sholley et al., 1984).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: miRNAs act cooperatively to give robustness to tip cell phenotype specification by reducing expression of cell-cycle progression genes.
source: Here, we show that in the initial step of SA, miRNAs act cooperatively to give robustness to the specification of the tip cell phenotype by reducing the expression of genes that are associated with cell-cycle progression and of members of the mitogen-associated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade that sustains VEGF-A-mediated cell proliferation
evidence: This is a summary inference drawn from the network analysis and experimental validations.

claim: miRNAs de-repress genes involved in cell migration and extracellular matrix remodeling during tip cell specification.
source: while de-repressing genes that are involved in cell migration and extracellular matrix remodeling.
evidence: This is a summary inference drawn from the network analysis showing downregulated miRNAs targeting upregulated genes.

claim: Target-site conservation is an indication of functional repression for mammalian miRNAs.
source: Considering that target-site conservation is believed to be an indication of functional repression for mammalian miRNAs (Friedman et al., 2009)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: RAF1 targeting by miR-497 inhibits breast cancer cell growth.
source: In particular, and in accordance with the interactions presented in this work, RAF1 targeting by miR-497 inhibits breast cancer cell growth (Li et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Downregulation of miR-424 leads to aberrant cell proliferation through MEK1 upregulation in senile hemangioma.
source: whereas downregulation of miR-424 leads to aberrant cell proliferation through MEK1 (MAP2K1) upregulation in senile hemangioma (Nakashima et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Previous studies attributed angiogenesis defects induced by DICER inhibition to reduction of VEGF-induced proliferation.
source: In fact, previous studies attributed the angiogenesis defects induced by DICER inhibition to a reduction of VEGF-induced proliferation (Suárez et al., 2007; Suárez et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The activation of ECs that enables tip cell selection and migration benefits from miRNA-mediated inhibition of cell proliferation.
source: However, the mechanistic demonstration of this hypothesis was limited to in vitro experiments that used 2D-cultured ECs only. Although we confirmed the reported effects of DICER inhibition in 2D cultures, we also demonstrated that the activation of ECs that enables tip cell selection and migration (the first step in SA [Carmeliet and Jain, 2011]) benefits from a miRNA-mediated inhibition of cell proliferation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing 2D and 3D experimental results with DICER knockdown.

claim: miR-424–5p upregulation reduced VEGF-induced proliferation in 2D EC cultures.
source: Earlier studies in two-dimensional EC cultures reported that miR-424–5p upregulation reduced VEGF-induced proliferation (Chamorro-Jorganes et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: miR-424–5p indirectly modulated HIF-α expression thus promoting angiogenesis.
source: or indirectly modulated HIF-α expression thus promoting angiogenesis (Ghosh et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: miR-29a inhibition impaired cell-cycle progression in 2D EC cultures.
source: whereas miR-29a inhibition impaired cell-cycle progression (Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: A widespread feature of miRNA activity toward a specific target is context-dependency.
source: However, it is also known that a widespread feature of miRNA activity toward a specific target is context-dependency, which also highlights the importance of target validation under physiological conditions (Erhard et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: A single miRNA can act on different targets belonging to the same pathway to reinforce its biological effect.
source: Our independent analyses in ECs support the concept that a single miRNA can act on different targets belonging to the same pathway to reinforce its biological effect.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the network analysis showing multiple targets per miRNA in specific pathways.

claim: Perturbation of miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p expression levels propagated throughout the network, causing alterations in expression of many other miRNAs.
source: In fact, perturbation of miR-424–5p and miR-29a-3p expression levels propagated throughout the network, causing alterations in the expression levels of a large number of other miRNAs, including miRNAs that share coding targets with miR-424–5p or mir-29a-3p.
evidence: This is supported by TaqMan array data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Each gene in the network is targeted by several different miRNAs.
source: Considering that each gene in the network is targeted by several different miRNAs, such broad network rearrangement could explain why inhibition of a single miRNA did not result in a significant increase in the expression of all its targets in a predictable way
evidence: This is inferred from the network structure shown in Figure 4 where genes have multiple miRNA inputs.

claim: Angiogenesis plays an important role in colorectal cancer progression.
source: This type of tumor was chosen because angiogenesis plays an important role in its progression (Battaglin et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Some colorectal cancer patients benefit from anti-angiogenic therapy with bevacizumab.
source: and some of the patients benefit from anti-angiogenic therapy with the VEGF blocker bevacizumab.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge.

claim: Network analysis of transcriptomic data from an in vitro SA model identified miRNA-mediated regulatory modules that fine-tune EC response to VEGF-A.
source: In summary, network analysis of whole transcriptomic data obtained from an in vitro SA model identified miRNA-mediated regulatory modules that fine-tune the response of ECs to VEGF-A and that could be exploited to identify new druggable biomarkers in angiogenesis-related diseases.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings supported by all the data presented.
